localBiteReport: As of the week of October 23, 2026, the Choctawhatchee Bay inshore fishery is in solid fall form. Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters reports that the redfish bite on the bay's flats held up well through a recent hurricane — the bay took on a tannin-stained tint rather than heavy mud, and sight-fishing visibility on the Destin-area flats remained fishable. Smaller slot and sub-slot reds (roughly 23 inches and under) are still working familiar guts, potholes, and shallow grass areas, while larger fish are beginning to shift into a more mobile fall pattern ahead of their eventual winter push toward creek mouths and river systems. A Fort Walton Beach-area guide posted to captainexperiences.com about a week ago noting that redfish and trout are heating up in the bayous — consistent with the seasonal fall feeding push underway. Water temperature at this location is currently 77°F. Sheepshead are expected to begin building on bridge and jetty structure as the month closes out, and a Santa Rosa Beach captain noted on captainexperiences.com that redfish are working docks and drop-offs while a few trout remain active — with the sheepshead bite expected to pick up in coming weeks. Note: the Half Hitch Destin report dated 10-19-26 appears in their site's recent-posts sidebar but its content was not retrievable via search; the most recent Half Hitch report with readable content is from 9-28-26.
